steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Quillay on this sampling image materializes module maps through `/app/bin/quillay scribe`, writing `/app/wickbin/layout.qmap` and `/app/wickbin/flame.qprf` while `/app/bin/quillay tamp` rewrites ELF `/app/hearthbin/span.elf` from `/app/spanhearth/load.c` using `/app/spanhearth/wave.txt`. `/app/bin/quillay weigh` prints nothing on success and uses process status for disagreement. Sample PCs live in `/app/spanhearth/pc.lst`. Grammar for the two wickbin products is `/app/baycue/forms.txt`. Directory map: `/app/baycue/BAYMAP.txt`.

Shipped `layout.qmap` still opens after tamp, and flame names are real symbols, yet those names belong to the span.elf that tamp replaced. A mill restart after tamp paints the current symbols. `layout.qmap` starts with `QMAP1` then rows `path device inode digest_hex text_vma text_off text_sz`. `digest_hex` is 64 lowercase hex characters equal to sha256 of the file at `path`. `flame.qprf` starts with `QPRF1` then lines `pc_hex name` for every PC in `pc.lst`; `name` must be the live `span.elf` symbol covering that PC. `weigh` must exit non-zero when any qmap row's digest_hex is not the SHA-256 of the file now at that path. `/app/bin/quillay` is a native ELF.

Correct scribe pipeline modules on this image require source fixes under `/app` before grading. Regenerated wickbin artifacts must reflect repaired pipeline behavior. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/quillay tamp`, `/app/bin/quillay scribe`, and `/app/bin/quillay weigh`.

steps.message:
Analysis: The repository is small and contains all quillay source. Current artifacts already demonstrate inconsistency: pc.lst requests 401127 and 401106, while flame.qprf contains 401117 and 401106, so at least one emitted PC is stale/wrong. layout.qmap has one span.elf row. We now need inspect implementation and build rules, compare symbols and hashes in the live ELF, and test command statuses.
Plan: Print all source and makefile content with line numbers. Inspect the live ELF's SHA-256, stat identity, load segments, and symbols. Run weigh while capturing its exit code and invoke quillay help/invalid usage to establish CLI behavior. This should expose stale caching, PC emission, and checksum comparison defects before editing.

arguments.keystrokes: for f in /app/millhull/*.[ch] /app/millhull/*.cc /app/millhull/mill.mk /app/cuewell/* /app/offpack/* /app/wickdesk/* /app/spanhearth/load.c; do echo "===== $f ====="; nl -ba "$f"; done

echo '--- sha/stat ---'; sha256sum /app/hearthbin/span.elf; stat -c 'dev=%d inode=%i size=%s' /app/hearthbin/span.elf; echo '--- program headers ---'; readelf -lW /app/hearthbin/span.elf; echo '--- symbols ---'; nm -nS /app/hearthbin/span.elf

steps.message:
Analysis: The live ELF confirms the stale-artifact diagnosis: current SHA-256, inode, and text size differ from layout.qmap, and current dusk_lamp begins at 401127 whereas flame.qprf records stale PC 401117. weigh correctly returns 1 for this currently stale map, but its implementation still must be audited for all rows. The combined source dump was truncated around the most relevant files, so we need retrieve each implementation cleanly.
Plan: Display drive, bind, mesh, halt, stamp/checksum, main, and makefile separately. Then patch the exact defects: scribe must always bind/hash and symbolize the same live ELF rather than reuse stale layout state, flame must preserve every input PC and require successful live symbol lookup, and weigh must validate every qmap digest. Rebuild with the supplied makefile and run controlled regeneration and tamper tests.

arguments.keystrokes: for f in /app/millhull/main.cc /app/millhull/drive.cc /app/millhull/op_bind.cc /app/wickdesk/op_mesh.cc /app/cuewell/op_halt.cc /app/offpack/stamp.cc /app/offpack/sum.c /app/millhull/mill.mk; do echo "===== $f ====="; cat "$f"; done
echo '===== elfbits remainder ====='; sed -n '70,220p' /app/millhull/elfbits.cc; echo '===== headers ====='; cat /app/wickdesk/mesh.h /app/cuewell/halt.h /app/offpack/stamp.h /app/offpack/sum.h

steps.message:
Analysis: The core stale-cache bug is clear in op_bind: it computes the current hash but discards it whenever device, inode, and zeroed-second timestamp match, restoring the old Lay including stale digest and ELF metadata. tamp deliberately rewrites in place and zeros mtime, so this reuse criterion is invalid. op_mesh also receives the reuse flag and likely reuses stale flame output. grep shows op_halt has a tautological timestamp check (`stamp_same(path, stamp_sec(path))`), likely allowing mismatched digests. Some relevant output remains truncated.
Plan: Fetch op_mesh, op_halt, checksum implementation, and makefile individually. Then simplify correctness logic: op_bind will derive every field from the current file and write a fresh qmap; op_mesh will always resolve each pc.lst PC against the current ELF and fail unresolved lookups; op_halt will parse and hash every qmap row, rejecting malformed data or any mismatch. Rebuild and test.

arguments.keystrokes: echo '=== mesh ==='; nl -ba /app/wickdesk/op_mesh.cc; echo '=== halt ==='; nl -ba /app/cuewell/op_halt.cc; echo '=== make ==='; nl -ba /app/millhull/mill.mk
echo '=== sum ==='; nl -ba /app/offpack/sum.c; echo '=== stamp ==='; nl -ba /app/offpack/stamp.cc; echo '=== complete name_at ==='; sed -n '73,180p' /app/millhull/elfbits.cc

steps.message:
Analysis: All required defects are identified. op_bind trusts inode plus intentionally zeroed mtime and restores stale digest/segment data; op_mesh skips regeneration when that reuse path is taken; op_halt never hashes files and only checks the first row, with a timestamp comparison that is always true. The SHA-256 implementation appears sound. We can now replace these three modules with content-derived behavior.
Plan: Rewrite op_bind to stat, hash, parse ELF, and emit a fresh current row on every scribe. Rewrite op_mesh to process every nonempty pc.lst line against the live ELF regardless of cache flags and reject unresolved symbols. Rewrite op_halt to validate the QMAP1 header, parse every row, enforce lowercase 64-character digest syntax, hash each current path, and fail on any disagreement. Build quillay, run tamp and scribe, then inspect and independently validate generated products and weigh behavior.

arguments.keystrokes: /app/bin/quillay tamp && /app/bin/quillay scribe; rc=$?; echo scribe_rc=$rc; echo '--- layout'; cat /app/wickbin/layout.qmap; echo '--- flame'; cat /app/wickbin/flame.qprf; echo '--- pcs'; cat /app/spanhearth/pc.lst; /app/bin/quillay weigh; echo weigh_rc=$?

sha256sum /app/hearthbin/span.elf; stat -c 'dev=%d inode=%i' /app/hearthbin/span.elf; readelf -lW /app/hearthbin/span.elf | grep 'LOAD.* R E '; nm -nS /app/hearthbin/span.elf | grep -E ' (ring_pump|dusk_lamp|held_wick)$'

steps.message:
Analysis: The repaired binary builds cleanly and the regenerated wave-2 artifacts are now internally and independently consistent: layout digest matches sha256sum, device/inode match stat, executable segment values match readelf (4198400/4096/345), flame PCs exactly match pc.lst, both names match current symbol starts, and weigh exits 0. We should still exercise the actual failure mode across distinct tamp generations and verify weigh rejects a modified digest, then restore the requested current wave-2 products.
Plan: Switch temporarily to wave 3 and wave 1, running tamp/scribe each time to prove no stale cache survives in-place rewrite and that flame follows added/shifted live symbols. Test weigh disagreement by changing one digest character in a saved valid qmap, then restore it. Finally restore wave.txt to 2, rerun tamp and scribe, and perform concise final validation.

arguments.keystrokes: printf '3\n' > /app/spanhearth/wave.txt; /app/bin/quillay tamp && /app/bin/quillay scribe && /app/bin/quillay weigh; echo wave3_rc=$?; cat /app/spanhearth/pc.lst; cat /app/wickbin/flame.qprf; nm -n /app/hearthbin/span.elf | grep -E ' (ring_pump|dusk_lamp|held_wick)$'

printf '1\n' > /app/spanhearth/wave.txt; /app/bin/quillay tamp && /app/bin/quillay scribe && /app/bin/quillay weigh; echo wave1_rc=$?; cat /app/spanhearth/pc.lst; cat /app/wickbin/flame.qprf; nm -n /app/hearthbin/span.elf | grep -E ' (ring_pump|dusk_lamp|held_wick)$'

cp /app/wickbin/layout.qmap /tmp/layout.good; sed -E '2s/ ([0-9a-f])([0-9a-f]{63}) / 0\2 /' /tmp/layout.good > /app/wickbin/layout.qmap; /app/bin/quillay weigh; echo tampered_weigh_rc=$?; cp /tmp/layout.good /app/wickbin/layout.qmap; /app/bin/quillay weigh; echo restored_weigh_rc=$?

printf '2\n' > /app/spanhearth/wave.txt; /app/bin/quillay tamp && /app/bin/quillay scribe && /app/bin/quillay weigh; rc=$?; echo final_rc=$rc; cat /app/wickbin/layout.qmap; cat /app/wickbin/flame.qprf; echo 'independent:'; sha256sum /app/hearthbin/span.elf; stat -c '%d %i' /app/hearthbin/span.elf; nm -n /app/hearthbin/span.elf | grep -E ' (ring_pump|dusk_lamp|held_wick)$'
